name: Autonomous Parking Operations
tagline: Keep a high-traffic facility stable while capacity changes underneath it.
brief: Build a load-aware controller for arrival surges, bay closures, charging failures, constrained lanes, and exit-gate outages.
context: Closures and capacity events occur without pausing the controller; inbound assignments may need automatic rerouting before they reach a bay.
narrative: ParkFlow now operates airport and event facilities. Traffic is bursty, category capacity changes during maintenance, and exit gates may fail while bays remain occupied. Shared lanes impose back-pressure: too many simultaneous movements increase future travel time. Priority vehicles may overtake the queue, but low-priority vehicles cannot be starved until their patience expires. Hard violations are forbidden; using a non-preferred but compatible bay is allowed at a satisfaction penalty.
objective: Adapt to every visible incident, preserve safety, prevent starvation, recover after closures, and pass an unseen suite of oscillating capacity and surge scenarios.
learningObjective: Design a load-aware scheduler that balances throughput, service priority, fairness, category preservation, and recovery.
intelligenceExplanation: The interview starts with no control rules. Build a flow around live queue pressure, patience, lane saturation, gate availability, hard category eligibility, and recovery after capacity incidents.
hint: Treat exits as capacity recovery, hard compatibility as eligibility, and VIP/EV placement as preferences. Use waiting time to prevent priority starvation.
hints: When the exit queue grows, each waiting departure is also an unavailable bay.
A closed preferred category may recover later, but the head vehicle's patience determines whether waiting is defensible.
Avoid reacting to congestion by continuously starting more entry movements.
